source.title: Compression Scaling Laws:Unifying Sparsity and Quantization
source.authors: Elias Frantar; Utku Evci; Wonpyo Park; N. Houlsby; Dan Alistarh

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether scaling-law behavior extends to compressed pretraining with weight quantization, weight-and-activation quantization, and sparsity.
record.gate_note: The paper reports scaling sweeps, fitted effective-parameter multipliers, and a data-independence comparison. The learning-rate sweep and tuning-table comparisons are not included as scaling-law results. Findings cited from earlier work are not recorded as results.
record.test_reason: The study fits a Chinchilla-form loss law with an effective-parameter multiplier to model-size sweeps of compressed pretraining (weight-only quantization, weight-and-activation quantization, mixed bit-widths, sparsity). Validation loss is reported for Llama-type models on a C4 variant. It asks whether the power-law form holds in a new training regime, so it is T3 for V5. Its dense 16-bit sweeps also bear weakly on V1.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. Add these points: 4-bit may be optimal for full quantization under their methods. 50% sparsity roughly matches 8w8a (0.871 vs 0.857), while quantization is more efficient than sparsity at higher compression. Compression effectiveness is said to grow with longer training, but this rests on prior work rather than this paper's results.
record.recipe_differences: Uses validation-loss scaling sweeps and a power-law form with an effective-parameter multiplier, but adds compression-aware training and compares compression types rather than reproducing the original dense-model parameter, token, and compute sweeps.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that full-quantization fit quality and efficiency vary with bit-width and with linear versus quadratic speedup counting. It also says sparsity multipliers are approximately 10% better than in earlier work, plausibly due to a better optimized setup, while describing them as relatively stable across setup changes.

fits_no_version.finding: Fitted effective parameter multipliers: weight-only 0.923/0.702/0.466 at 4/2/1-bit; full quantization 0.857/0.747/0.289/0.067 at 8/4/2/1-bit; sparsity 0.871/0.622 at 50%/75%. These measure how much each compressed parameter is worth, not whether loss follows a power law.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Compression acts as a constant multiplier on effective parameter count in LM scaling laws, and its size depends on the compression type and level.

fits_no_version.finding: Sparsity size-gain multipliers are about 10% better than in Frantar et al. 2024, and the authors describe them as relatively stable across setup changes.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Compression multipliers are stable across training setups.

record.problems: Most loss-scaling results are presented in figures without tabulated values, and the text does not state the model-size range. Experiments focus on Llama-type models and a variant of C4. No uncertainty estimates are reported.
record.rows_left_out: The learning-rate sweep in Figure 1 and tuning results in Tables 1 and 4 are omitted because they concern hyperparameter or sparsity-method tuning rather than reported scaling-law outcomes.

untested.parts: Token and compute sweeps (data is fixed at Chinchilla ratios, so the D term is not separately identified). A range of several orders of magnitude (only about one decade is shown). Fitted exponents are not reported.
Prediction of runs orders of magnitude larger; only a 2x-data check is made.
Compute-optimal allocation is not swept; Chinchilla ratios are assumed.
Shape at fixed parameter count is not tested.
Other modalities, repeated data, fine-tuning and transfer; only compressed text pretraining is tested.
No comparison of exponents or compute-optimal splits across fitting choices; no test of curvature away from a single power law.

missing.what: Fitted law coefficients (a, b, c, d, e) and the model-size range in parameters; neither is given in the text, only the figure axes.

record.verdict_notes: Several dense rows (R3, R10, R21, R26) probably replot the same dense runs. The fit varies only N at fixed Chinchilla ratios, so the data term is not identified. 'Pareto optimal' statements concern efficiency, not the law's validity, so rows R13 and R15 were changed from partial to observed. The paper is a short technical report preprint with no uncertainty estimates.

versions.untested_parts: Tests parameter-size scaling in compressed Llama-type pretraining, with tokens-per-parameter following Chinchilla ratios. Does not independently sweep tokens or compute, establish several orders of magnitude, or test the uncompressed law across all three variables.
The 1x-to-2x Chinchilla comparison checks data independence of fitted multipliers, not whether fits on small runs predict runs orders of magnitude larger.
Uses Chinchilla ratios but does not sweep compute budgets to find loss-minimising parameter and token allocations.
Does not compare depth, width, or architecture choices at fixed parameter count.
Tests compressed text pretraining only; does not test other modalities, repeated data, fine-tuning, or transfer.
Reports validation loss, not downstream-task performance or its predictability.

Does not test dependence of the original scaling exponents or compute-optimal split on fitting choices, nor whether curves bend away from a single power law. It notes a roughly 10% change in sparsity size-gain multipliers relative to earlier work, but does not compare fitted exponents or allocations.

relationships.condition: Dense 16-bit Llama-type models on a C4 variant at Chinchilla ratios, over about one decade of size
relationships.reason: The dense baseline sweeps (R3, R10, R21, R26) lie on the fitted law form. The evidence is figure only, with a narrow range and no exponents reported.
relationships.display_finding: Dense 16-bit baseline losses aligned with the fitted scaling law over about one decade of model size.

relationships.condition: Compressed pretraining: weight-only quantization (4/2/1-bit), full quantization at 8/4/2-bit, mixed bit-widths, and 50%/75% sparsity
relationships.reason: The text reports clear trends, a very good sparsity fit and expected mixed-width behaviour. The 1x-fitted law also predicts the 2x-data runs (R1, R2, R4-R6, R11-R13, R15, R22-R25, R27, R28).
relationships.display_finding: The law described quantization and mixed-width trends, fitted sparsity well, and predicted runs using twice the data from fits using the original data volume.

relationships.reason: The authors say the full-quantization fit is less clean, and reasonable 'especially for more than 1-bit', implying a weaker fit at 1 bit (R14, R16).
relationships.display_finding: Full weight-and-activation quantization produced less clean fits, with the authors describing agreement as better above 1 bit.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Weight-only quantization, sparsity, mixed bit-widths, and full quantization above 1 bit in the tested Llama-type pretraining setup
reader_labels.reason: The authors report clear weight-only scaling trends, a very good sparsity fit, expected mixed-quantization behavior, and a reasonable full-quantization fit; see R3-R13 and R17-R30.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: The full-quantization fit is described as less clean than weight-only quantization, and effectiveness drops sharply below 4 bits; see R13-R16 and R19-R20.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Compressed text pretraining using weight-only quantization, sparsity, mixed quantization, and full quantization above 1 bit
reader_labels.reason: The tested compression-based pretraining settings show the reported scaling behavior, though the paper does not test other modalities or the other regimes named in this version; see R3-R13 and R17-R30.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: The authors describe diminished returns at lower bit-widths and a less clean fit for full quantization; see R13-R16 and R19-R20.
